title: ai_transcript_audit plugin config
description: The `config` object of an enabled `ai_transcript_audit` plugin, generated from ferrum-edge/ferrum-edge openapi.yaml at v0.9.21 (f9915358c8032214f4034a17c28cdf72d14006c3), component AiTranscriptAuditConfig and every component it references. Do not edit: run ci/plugin_config_schemas.py. This is Edge's own configuration schema, governed by Edge's support policy (docs/versioning.md); the plugin catalog records when Edge requires it.

AiTranscriptAuditConfig.description: Plugin: ai_transcript_audit — Controlled AI payload capture for compliance/audit. Priority 2740 runs after authentication/authorization and before request_deduplication (3010); local/Redis replays emit one record with cache.request_deduplication.replayed=true, and priority overrides that reverse the order are rejected. Captures AI request/response bodies (after redaction), keyed HMAC-SHA256 body hashes (keyed with redaction.hash_secret when set, else a per-process random key), model/provider, token metadata, guardrail decisions (including bounded ai_tool_governor.* fields), tool names, and allow-listed cache telemetry (namespaced `ai_semantic_cache.<id>.{cache_status,cache_match,cache_similarity}` and `request_deduplication.replayed`; never `cache_key`), then exports them asynchronously to an HTTPS collector in batches. Capture excerpt limits each have a deployment-safe hard maximum of 1048576 bytes and a cross-field aggregate maximum of 2097152; request-derived model/tool metadata is independently bounded (256/64/128/4096) before staging. Retention is bounded by BOTH record count (sink.buffer_capacity) and an aggregate retained-byte budget (limits.buffer_max_bytes / limits.max_entry_bytes) covering staged candidates, fail-closed pre-commit reservations, active fail-open stream capture, exact pre-serialized queue payloads, JSON-array assembly, and every sequential retry. A fail-open stream reserves the maximum retained-record charge before copying response bytes and transfers that lease at terminal enqueue; a fail-closed stream reuses its pre-commit lease. Retry clones share immutable Bytes rather than deep-cloning records; reqwest receives the already-escaped exact-capacity JSON body rather than reserializing it. In redacted_body, limits.max_redaction_scan_bytes is checked before JSON classification/model/tool extraction/redaction; oversized JSON POSTs are conservatively audited as possible streaming AI requests with explicit omission evidence rather than bypassing audit. Streamed keyed hashing is bounded by capture.stream_hash, and active-stream reservations by limits.max_stream_reservation_secs. Authenticated /health exposes effective admitted ceilings plus live retained_bytes/retained_byte_drops/stream_reservations_expired/sink_healthy gauges without transcript content. Never blocks or rejects the proxy hot path unless an operator opts into a fail-closed policy (sink.on_buffer_full=reject or sink.on_sink_error=reject); those policies also apply to request-only and conservatively classified oversized capture. In-flight staging is hard-bounded at 4096 entries per plugin instance while candidate/record_id/sample markers remain shared across co-located instances: a saturated instance neither erases a peer's live candidate nor borrows it for response buffering, response hooks, stream reservations, sampling/admission, or record emission. The local staging entry is consumed by atomic removal at buffered or ordinary stream-terminal commit. Expiry first revokes capture/hash work and releases all staging/queue/byte owners; its single-fire request-owned terminal slot carries only the local sampling roll needed for a body-free best-effort fallback and cannot be created from shared peer markers. Orphan/reservation sweeps are time-gated. Not a security boundary on its own — pair with ai_prompt_shield, ai_semantic_firewall, ai_response_guard, and ai_tool_governor for enforcement. HTTP by default; native gRPC capture requires an explicit descriptor-based grpc enrollment block (enrolled methods only). Unknown keys are rejected at the root and every fixed nested object (capture, sampling, redaction, custom_patterns items, limits, privacy, sink); sink.custom_headers remains the only intentional free-form string map. Outbound sink header values are literal text plus optional ${secret:NAME} references scoped to the FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_* env namespace (no generic process-environment interpolation), fully materialized and validated when the background worker activates so a missing/empty/invalid secret fails activation instead of sending unauthenticated. privacy.path_mode governs request-path export; a privacy mode never exports the literal path by default. Nested objects may be omitted or null to keep defaults. Redacted captures replace malformed function.arguments JSON with [UNPARSEABLE] and set arguments_redaction_failed=true on the captured function object; valid arguments retain member-name redaction. Explicit full_body raw capture is unchanged. Every fixed scalar whose runtime default is used when the key is omitted also accepts an explicit null; the batching keys (sink.batch_size, sink.flush_interval_ms, sink.buffer_capacity, sink.max_retries, sink.retry_delay_ms), sink.endpoint_url, sink.custom_headers, redaction.custom_patterns, grpc, grpc.descriptor_path, and grpc.methods do NOT — null is a type error for those, exactly as the schema states. RUNTIME-ONLY CHECKS this component deliberately cannot express, all of which still reject the configuration at construction: (1) arithmetic relationships between limits — limits.max_entry_bytes must be >= the worst-case serialized-JSON contract implied by the configured capture limits, limits.buffer_max_bytes must be >= both 65536 and the retained charge of limits.max_entry_bytes, and max_request_bytes + max_response_bytes + max_stream_capture_bytes must be <= 2097152; (2) Rust `regex` crate compilation of every redaction.builtins entry and every redaction.custom_patterns[].regex, and rejection of an unknown redaction.builtins name beyond the enum; (3) sink.endpoint_url authority, userinfo, and backend-egress SSRF screening, plus the rule that cleartext http:// is admitted only with sink.allow_insecure_loopback: true AND a loopback IP-literal host (not the name localhost); (4) sink.custom_headers name/value validity and the ${secret:NAME} template grammar (a resolvable FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_<NAME> is checked later still, when the background worker activates); (5) node-local existence and decodability of grpc.descriptor_path, and resolution of each method's request_type / response_type / text_fields against that descriptor — Admin/CP admission validates shape only; (6) grpc.methods key normalization (trim plus one optional leading slash) and the rejection of two keys that normalize to the same method path; (7) grpc.methods[].text_fields segment trimming, the per-path segment-depth ceiling, and duplicate detection after normalization, which catches pairs that uniqueItems cannot ("a.b" versus "a . b"); and (8) the plugin-cache composition rule that refuses a priority override placing this instance at or after a co-located request_deduplication instance.

mode.description: Null keeps the default, as for every other fixed scalar here. metadata_only: keyed body hashes + model/provider/token/guardrail metadata, no body. redacted_body: capped, PII-redacted request/response excerpts. Values beneath normalized sensitive JSON keys (password/auth/cookie/session/credential/private-key/client-secret/API-key/token variants) are replaced regardless of value shape; everything under an Azure 'On Your Data' parameters object inside a data_sources / dataSources / data-sources container is additionally replaced wholesale, and recognizing that container name never short-circuits the ordinary visitor — a value under it that is not the provider's conventional array (object, string, number, boolean, null) is still traversed with the same member-name and pattern rules; JSON objects/arrays encoded inside strings (including tool arguments) are recursively decoded/redacted to a depth cap of 64. Uniform OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE is reassembled before redaction with exact shape {sse_reassembled:true,object:'chat.completion.chunk',completion_text:{'<choice>':'…'},tool_calls:{'<choice>':[{index,id,type,function:{name,arguments}}]},finish_reason:{'<choice>':'…'}}; absent categories are omitted, and text/tool fragments are concatenated by choice/tool index under max_stream_capture_bytes. Only a provider-declared unsigned index correlates fragments across deltas; array position is intra-delta identity only (exported as 'position:<n>' choice keys and a tool-call 'position' field, never as a fabricated index). Malformed optional fields do not abort reassembly (that would drop back to per-frame redaction, which cannot see a secret split across fragments): ignorable ones (finish_reason, delta, delta.content, tool_calls, id, type, function, function.name, function.arguments) are skipped, while a malformed identity-bearing index (choices[].index, tool_calls[].index) takes a collision-free per-occurrence bucket ('unattributed:<n>' choice key, index_unattributed:true plus occurrence:<n> on a tool call) rather than collapsing onto index 0, sharing one unattributed bucket, or being dropped. Where identity is a guess, payload is withheld instead of joined or split: ambiguous completion text becomes '[REDACTED:ambiguous_choice]' with choice_identity_ambiguous:true and completion_text_withheld:true, and ambiguous tool arguments become '[REDACTED:ambiguous_tool_call]' with arguments_withheld:true. Skipped or re-routed fields are listed in a sorted malformed_fields array of compiled-in field paths (never provider values); the key is omitted for well-formed streams. Other or non-parseable SSE stays per-event: each event's data lines are joined with a newline as a client reads them and redacted as one document, and a JSON-shaped event payload the parser refuses is replaced, continuation lines included, by one data: [UNPARSEABLE] line. A leading UTF-8 BOM is stripped before any structural parse; a request candidate or JSON-typed response that no structural parse can read (UTF-16/UTF-32, NaN, comments, a batch past the nesting limit) is never pattern-redacted, because sensitive member names need the parse: its excerpt is withheld with request_body_omitted_reason / response_body_omitted_reason unparseable_document. full_body: capped unredacted excerpts (requires allow_full_body). hash_only: keyed body hashes + envelope only. Body hashes are keyed HMAC-SHA256 in every mode, never plain SHA-256.

allow_full_body.description: Required guardrail for mode=full_body, which captures unredacted payloads. Construction fails if full_body is set without this opt-in.

capture.description: What to capture. Omit or null to keep defaults. At least one of request, response, or streaming_response must stay enabled.

streaming_response.description: Capture SSE response excerpts. false | true | 'sampled', or the string spellings 'true' / 'false', or null for the default. true forces every AI-candidate request's response onto the stream-inspection path. 'sampled' tees only requests that win the sampling.rate roll (or whose request-side guardrail fired when always_capture_on_guardrail is set — the tee decision is evaluated at dispatch time, after the request-phase guardrail plugins ran); error responses and response-side guardrail hits on un-sampled streaming requests still emit records via the log fallback, but without a response body/hash — teeing every stream to cover those late triggers would defeat sampled capture.

headers.description: Capture response headers (redacted by key). Also gated by privacy.include_raw_headers.

tool_calls.description: Extract tool/function names from the request body.

mcp_tool_calls.description: Treat MCP JSON-RPC tools/call requests (a singleton, or a batch with a tools/call member) as audit candidates for JSON-ish content types. Content-Type-less POSTs are buffered and captured when they carry a tools/call (a byte pre-scan skips parsing and staging for anything else); set capture.mcp_endpoint_path to limit this to one exact path; add an mcp section to records with the public tool name, keyed arguments_hash, optional excerpt, outcome, and bounded gateway metadata. At most 32 calls per record; later ones are counted in calls_omitted.

mcp_endpoint_path.description: Optional exact path that narrows Content-Type-less MCP capture. When unset, Content-Type-less POSTs on every path are buffered and checked for a tools/call; when set, only this path is. Set it to the mcp_gateway endpoint.path to avoid buffering other Content-Type-less uploads.

mcp_arguments.description: Add each MCP call's arguments excerpt, shaped like a body excerpt (redacted in redacted_body, raw in full_body) and sharing limits.max_request_bytes with the request excerpt. Requires mcp_tool_calls and mode redacted_body or full_body.

stream_hash.description: How much of a streamed (SSE) response the exported keyed HMAC-SHA256 response_hash covers. capped (default) stops hashing at limits.max_stream_capture_bytes, so limits.max_stream_capture_bytes bounds audit CPU as well as retained bytes and an indefinitely long high-bandwidth stream cannot keep a keyed hash running for the life of the connection; the digest is then marked response_hash_scope=partial, carries the exact response_hash_bytes it covered, and is domain-separated so it can never collide with or be presented as a full-stream digest. full is the explicit opt-in for deployments whose evidence chain genuinely re-derives the provider's complete response, and accepts unbounded per-byte keyed-hashing cost. The response_hash is a tamper-evidence/correlation token over the captured transcript, not an integrity attestation of the client's byte stream — abnormally terminated and downstream-cut streams already omit it entirely. Buffered (non-streamed) responses are complete by construction and always hash full.

sampling.description: Sampling controls. Omit or null to keep defaults.

rate.description: Fraction of eligible AI transactions emitted as full records. Guardrail/error captures override the roll.

always_capture_on_guardrail.description: Override a losing sampling roll for a fired guardrail. A non-empty ai_tool_governor.decision other than allow (deny, dry_run, require_approval, or redact_args) fires this override on request, buffered-response, and terminal-stream paths; ordinary allow does not. Exported guardrails include bounded ai_tool_governor.enabled, mode, decision, tool_names, risk, policy_ids, approval_id, and redacted_tools fields. The governor's ai_tool_governor.arguments_hashes (an unkeyed SHA-256 of each call's arguments, an offline guessing oracle) is never exported; mcp.calls[].arguments_hash is the keyed equivalent.

always_capture_on_error.description: Override a losing sampling roll for a failed transaction. Fires on an HTTP status >= 400, on a streamed body that did not complete, and on the final client-visible gRPC application status: a native gRPC call normally fails under HTTP 200 with a non-zero grpc-status, and that status (from the terminal trailers, a Trailers-Only header block, or the UNKNOWN a gRPC transaction with no terminal status carries) is treated as an error at buffered commit, stream termination, and the transaction-log fallback alike. grpc-status 0 remains a success and stays subject to ordinary sampling.

max_records_per_minute.description: Records-per-minute cap (0 = unlimited). Over the cap, records are dropped and traffic is NEVER rejected: a record the window has already refused takes no queue permit or retained-byte reservation and cannot select a fail-closed 503, so sink.on_buffer_full/on_sink_error: reject cannot deny traffic for an audit record that could not have been written. Suppression is bounded by the window — the first record admitted after it rolls over flushes normally, which is the same background-send recovery probe that restores sink health elsewhere. The admitted maximum is the unsigned 64-bit ceiling (a larger literal is a type error, not a clamp); the effective in-window ceiling is clamped to 4294967294.

redaction.description: PII redaction policy for captured excerpts. Omit or null to keep defaults. In mode=redacted_body and mode=metadata_only the pattern set must not be empty: builtins=[] with no custom_patterns is rejected at construction (a pass-through redactor would export unredacted data — body excerpts in redacted_body, the request-derived model/tool_names in both — without the full_body opt-in; hash_only exports no request-derived strings and is exempt). redacted_body also replaces values beneath normalized sensitive parent keys and recursively redacts JSON-encoded object/array strings before applying regex patterns.

builtins.description: Built-in PII patterns, shared with ai_prompt_shield/ai_response_guard. Omit or null for the default set; an explicit empty array with no custom_patterns is refused in redacted_body/metadata_only, and under privacy.path_mode: redact in every mode.

placeholder.description: Non-hashing replacement template; {type} is substituted with the pattern name.

hash_redacted_values.description: Replace matches with [REDACTED:<type>:<hmac-prefix>] so identical values stay correlatable without storing the raw value. The digest is a keyed HMAC-SHA256 (see hash_secret), never a plain hash — most PII value spaces are small enough to brute-force offline from an unsalted digest.

hash_secret.description: Optional key for the redacted-value HMAC and the exported request/response body hashes. The minimum length is counted in CHARACTERS (Unicode code points), matching this minLength — not in UTF-8 bytes, so a 16-character multi-byte secret is refused even though it carries 32 bytes. When set (min 32 characters), hashed placeholders and body hashes are stable across gateway instances and restarts, so values correlate fleet-wide. When omitted or null, each process generates a random key at startup: digests still correlate within one process lifetime but never across restarts/instances, and can never be dictionary-attacked from exported records. Treat like any other secret — do not log or export it.

limits.description: Capture size caps for request/response/stream excerpts. Each field has a deployment-safe hard maximum (1048576). The sum of all three must be <= 2097152 so a valid combination cannot retain an unsafe aggregate body budget. Request-derived model/tool metadata is bounded independently of these excerpt settings (model <= 256 bytes, <= 64 tool names, each name <= 128 bytes, aggregate tool-name bytes <= 4096). Omit or null to keep defaults.

max_request_bytes.description: Maximum retained request-body excerpt bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate with max_response_bytes and max_stream_capture_bytes.

max_response_bytes.description: Maximum retained buffered response-body excerpt bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate.

max_stream_capture_bytes.description: Maximum retained SSE stream-capture bytes. Hard maximum 1048576. Counts toward the cross-field aggregate. Also bounds the streamed keyed digest unless capture.stream_hash is full.

max_redaction_scan_bytes.description: Independent hard processing bound for redacted-mode request classification, model/tool extraction, and body shaping. In mode=redacted_body the raw length is checked before serde_json: payloads above this bound are never JSON-parsed, model/tool scanned, redaction-scanned, or copied into an excerpt. An oversized POST application/json is conservatively audited as a possible AI request and treated as potentially streaming (so capture does not buffer a possibly unbounded SSE response); parse-derived model/tool fields are omitted and fail-closed queue/byte admission still applies. The record carries request_body_omitted_reason / response_body_omitted_reason = redaction_scan_limit with the body_truncated flag set. Hashes, envelope, status, and bounded guardrail metadata still export. Streaming redacted capture enforces this bound while chunks arrive: if it is smaller than max_stream_capture_bytes, no more than max_redaction_scan_bytes is copied and crossing the bound records response_body_omitted_reason = redaction_scan_limit rather than exporting a raw boundary fragment. The keyed digest still follows capture.stream_hash until reservation expiry revokes all audit work. mode=full_body caps on a UTF-8 boundary first and never scans past the cap, so it is unaffected.

max_entry_bytes.description: Maximum serialized JSON bytes for one admitted record. Queue admission first performs an allocation-free bounded counting serialization, then serializes into one exact-capacity immutable Bytes payload. The default/minimum is derived from the configured capture limits and worst-case JSON escaping: 6 * (max_request_bytes + max(max_response_bytes, max_stream_capture_bytes) + 256 + 4096 + 8192). The hard maximum is 16777216. A complete record whose bounded envelope still exceeds this ceiling is dropped/rejected, never partially serialized.

buffer_max_bytes.description: Aggregate retained-byte budget for one plugin instance, covering staged request candidates, fail-closed pre-commit reservations, active fail-open stream capture, immutable pre-serialized queue payloads, one exact-capacity JSON-array request body, and every sequential retry. sink.buffer_capacity bounds the RECORD COUNT only; without this budget a slow collector can retain capacity x attacker-shaped record bytes. Retry clones share Bytes and do not deep-clone transcript fields; reqwest does not reserialize the batch. The exact per-record lease is 2 * (serialized_record_bytes + 1) + 128. Admission is (count AND bytes) and is enforced atomically before publication; leases release on every completion, discard, TTL-sweep, reservation-expiry, and failed-batch path. Saturation follows sink.on_buffer_full (drop or reject). Must be at least 2 * (max_entry_bytes + 1) + 128. Live retained_bytes and retained_byte_drops are exposed on authenticated /health.

max_stream_reservation_secs.description: Maximum lifetime of one active stream's staging entry and its reserved commit permit. An active stream is exempt from the one-hour orphan TTL, so without this bound a never-ending stream, or one whose terminal hook is lost, would hold a staging slot, a queue permit, and its retained bytes forever until all reservations were exhausted. The staging entry owns one cancellable single-fire deadline from first active response selection until staging is actually consumed or dropped. It revokes even an idle selection with no concrete inspector at its deadline without waiting for another request or chunk, and remains armed after normal inspector terminal claim while staging is retained for the immediate transaction-log fallback. Normal staging consumption wakes and cancels the task promptly; the amortized sweep remains a repair net. Both paths dynamically resolve and first revoke any current per-stream response accumulator and keyed HMAC through narrowly scoped shared state, then release the queue permit, staging slot, staging lease, and worst-case queued-record lease exactly once. An atomic fired/cancelled token makes deadline, sweep, terminal, inspector-drop, and log-fallback races single-fire. Later bytes forward unchanged without capture or hash work. No global tombstone remains for the live connection: inspector drop publishes a body-free request-owned handoff only when the stream actually terminates. Normal or abnormal late termination emits at most one best-effort fallback without request/response excerpts or hashes and without resurrecting the released commit permit. The process-global live-slot map is capped at 4096 and expiry releases that capacity; the remaining stream-owned handle has no capture/hash/accounting state. Reclamations are logged and counted in stream_reservations_expired on authenticated /health.

sink.description: Async batched HTTPS sink. The endpoint is SSRF-screened against the backend egress policy at construction (literal IPs) and at send time (resolved hostnames). Cleartext HTTP requires allow_insecure_loopback=true and is then limited to a loopback IP literal (not the name localhost). Unknown sink keys are rejected; custom_headers remains an open string map.

endpoint_url.description: Collector URL. Only the http and https schemes are admitted (the pattern is spelled case-insensitively because URL schemes are). HTTPS is required by default. HTTP is accepted only for a loopback IP literal (127.0.0.0/8 or [::1], not the name localhost) when allow_insecure_loopback is explicitly true. Userinfo credentials (https://user:pass@host) are rejected — authenticate with custom_headers. A collector that requires a credential in the URL path or query is supported, and this value is never rendered in operational output: egress-denial, DNS/TLS, retry, slow-call, and batch-failure diagnostics show only a structurally redacted scheme://host:port/redacted form. The admin audit and non-admin read projections apply the schema-aware sensitivity contract instead, keeping only scheme://host[:port] with `[REDACTED_PATH]` / `[REDACTED_QUERY]` / `[REDACTED_FRAGMENT]` markers.

allow_insecure_loopback.description: Allow an http:// collector only when endpoint_url uses a loopback IP literal. The name localhost does not qualify: DNS overrides and the resolver decide where a name connects. This never permits remote cleartext delivery.

custom_headers.description: Extra headers sent on every batch. Arbitrary header names are accepted (the only intentional free-form map in the plugin config). Values are literal text plus optional ${secret:NAME} references, which resolve ONLY the FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_<NAME> environment namespace (e.g. Authorization: 'Bearer ${secret:AUDIT_TOKEN}' reads FERRUM_TRANSCRIPT_SINK_SECRET_AUDIT_TOKEN, composing with the _VAULT/_AWS/_AZURE/_GCP/_FILE external-secret suffixes). There is no generic ${ENV_VAR} process-environment interpolation, so unrelated Ferrum/database/cloud/system secrets cannot be exfiltrated into an outbound header; any other ${...} form, or a NAME outside [A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*, is rejected at config admission. Names/templates are validated at admission; secrets are materialized once when the background worker activates. A missing, empty, or invalid secret/header value fails activation (the generation is never published) rather than being silently omitted, so on_sink_error=reject is honored on the first request. Materialized secret values are marked sensitive and never logged.

retry_delay_ms.description: Fixed delay between batch send retries for transient collector failures.

on_buffer_full.description: drop: silently drop when the queue or per-instance 4096-entry staging bound is full (never block). reject: fail selected request-only, buffered, streaming, synthetic, or final-body-fallback audit records with 503 before dispatch/response commit when staging or a queue slot cannot be reserved. Either reject policy also claims the finalized request representation of candidate-shaped POSTs, so a Content-Encoding is decoded by the shared request representation gate before classification (an undecodable one is refused with 400), and any candidate body no parser can read (comments, UTF-16/UTF-32, NaN, trailing commas — independent of capture.mcp_tool_calls) is conservatively audited rather than forwarded unaudited. Shared candidate markers from co-located peers do not bypass this bound. Streaming admission honors sampling plus configured error/guardrail overrides.

on_sink_error.description: warn: log and drop on permanent sink failure. reject: fail selected request-only, buffered, streaming, synthetic, or final-body-fallback audit records with 503 before dispatch/response commit while the sink is unhealthy. Like on_buffer_full: reject, it claims the finalized representation of candidate-shaped POSTs (content codings decoded before classification, unreadable candidate bodies conservatively audited). Streaming admission honors sampling plus configured error/guardrail overrides. Sink health is published from the COMPLETE delivery outcome, never from response headers alone: the acknowledgement body is drained and validated under sink.ack_max_bytes / sink.ack_timeout_ms first, and a 2xx whose acknowledgement stalls, overruns its bound, fails transport, or fails ack_policy validation is an ambiguous delivery that marks the sink unhealthy AND returns the batch for retry. Any non-2xx collector response also marks the sink unhealthy — including non-retryable 4xx (401/403/413, e.g. an expired token) whose batch is discarded rather than retried — so records silently lost at the collector stop audited traffic instead of letting it flow unaudited. Hysteresis: health drops on the first failed or ambiguous delivery with no damping, and is restored only by a 2xx whose acknowledgement fully drained and validated; each retry attempt re-publishes, so recovery happens on the attempt that actually succeeded. Rejected transactions still build and enqueue their audit record — the background flush of those records is the recovery probe.

ack_policy.description: How a collector acknowledgement is validated before sink health is published. drain: read the acknowledgement to EOF under sink.ack_max_bytes and sink.ack_timeout_ms, discarding the bytes (content is not inspected). json: additionally require a JSON object that does not report rejected records — a non-object/unparseable body, a non-zero/non-empty errors|failed|rejected|error_count field, or a status string outside the unequivocal affirmative set ok|success|accepted|created fails the batch. Ambiguous partial-delivery values such as partial_ok are unhealthy even without an explicit failure count. Acknowledgement bytes are never retained beyond the bound and never logged; only compiled-in failure classes appear in diagnostics, so a hostile collector cannot echo captured transcript content back into gateway logs.

ack_max_bytes.description: Hard bound on the acknowledgement body read from the collector. An advertised Content-Length above this, or a stream that exceeds it, fails the batch instead of buffering unbounded collector output into the flush worker.

ack_timeout_ms.description: Maximum time spent draining/validating one acknowledgement after headers arrive. Separate from the plugin HTTP client request timeout so a stalled acknowledgement cannot pin a flush worker for the full request budget.

privacy.description: Identity/header/path export controls. Omit or null to keep defaults.

path_mode.description: How the request path is exported. Applications often embed emails/account-ids/document-names/tokens in path segments, so a privacy mode never exports the literal path by default. omit: no path. template: export the matched route identifier (proxy listen_path, else proxy name; omitted when unavailable) instead of the user-controlled path. redact: literal path with the configured PII redactor applied (requires at least one redaction.builtins/custom_patterns pattern). hash: keyed HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the literal path (shares redaction.hash_secret; not brute-forceable offline). raw: literal path verbatim. Default is template for metadata_only/redacted_body/hash_only and raw for full_body (the deliberate raw-capture opt-in).

grpc.description: Native-gRPC capture contract. Present means the plugin also applies to native gRPC, but only enrolled methods are decoded and captured. Because the backend-effective method is not authoritative until after routing, the presence of this block conservatively buffers every native-gRPC request on the proxy; unenrolled responses are not buffered by this plugin. Captured string fields honor the same mode/redaction contract as HTTP excerpts: in redacted_body a value is replaced wholesale when ANY enclosing name matches the sensitive field-name policy — the field itself, any ancestor message field, or the protobuf map key of a map entry (map keys are never exported as labels; each map value is exported under a collision-free ordinal path such as `metadata.0`, and the key still decides redaction) — every element of a repeated field inherits that field's own decision, and JSON embedded inside a protobuf string is decoded and redacted before export. Malformed, truncated, oversized, undecodable, or unknown-field payloads omit the excerpt with a compiled-in reason rather than exporting partial or unredacted bytes. Requires a node-local FileDescriptorSet; Admin/CP admission validates shape only, and mode-aware file-dependency validation resolves the descriptor on data-plane nodes. The enrolled method is the BACKEND-EFFECTIVE one, which is not known until after routing and listen-path stripping, so configuring this block fully buffers the request body of EVERY native gRPC request on the proxy — enrolled or not — and the final request-body hook makes the authoritative enrollment decision. An enrolled instance joins the backend-path boundary itself, so that decision uses the backend-effective path the proxy binds (its trailing /Service/Method) and does not require grpc_method_router; the bound path is never outranked by the plugin-writable grpc_full_method metadata. A call enrolled only by its backend-effective method is staged at that boundary, so a deferred before_proxy short circuit after it still leaves a record. A client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming method on such a proxy therefore gets fully buffered request semantics; max_messages caps how much is captured, not how much is buffered.

descriptor_path.description: Node-local path to a compiled protobuf FileDescriptorSet. Validated shape-only at Admin/CP admission and against the real descriptor by mode-aware file-dependency validation. A readable but invalid descriptor rejects the candidate configuration; an absent or unreadable descriptor retains enrollment and omits body excerpts at request time.

methods.description: Map of "/package.Service/Method" to that method's capture contract. Only these methods are captured. Leading/trailing whitespace and one optional leading slash are normalized by the runtime; every dotted service segment and the method identifier must be a protobuf/gRPC identifier. Duplicate normalized forms are rejected at runtime. Each entry must set request_type and/or response_type.

request_type.description: Fully-qualified protobuf request message type. Null (or a blank string) is treated exactly as absent, so the other direction must then be set.

response_type.description: Fully-qualified protobuf response message type. Null (or a blank string) is treated exactly as absent, so the other direction must then be set.

text_fields.description: Dotted field paths restricting which string fields are exported. Each path must end at a string field and may not traverse a map field. Repeated fields retain every selected value under indexed paths such as tags.0 or messages.2.text. Omit, or set null, to cover every string field recursively; an explicit empty array is refused. The runtime additionally trims each dotted segment before comparing, so it rejects duplicates uniqueItems cannot see ("a.b" versus "a . b"), rejects an empty segment, and rejects a path deeper than the message-nesting ceiling.

max_message_bytes.description: Per-message ceiling, applied to the declared frame length and enforced while inflating a gzip-compressed frame; inflation stops at the tighter of this ceiling and the remaining redaction-scan budget. Aggregate decoded payload across frames is additionally capped by limits.max_redaction_scan_bytes. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 8388608 (8 MiB), equal to the hard maximum of that aggregate scan ceiling — a larger per-message value could never produce a capture.

max_messages.description: Maximum number of length-prefixed frames one buffered gRPC request or response may carry; above this the excerpt is omitted rather than partially captured. Bounded by an immutable deployment maximum of 1024 frames: the decoded-byte scan budget bounds decoded payload, not frame count, so legal zero-length frames would otherwise let an operator-configured value drive an effectively unbounded frame vector. Descriptor-tree depth and node ceilings are aggregate across the complete buffered body, rather than resetting for every frame; exhaustion omits the complete excerpt with grpc_scan_limit.
